ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every beneficial owner, director, and authorized shareholder must be screened within 90 days before filing against the Financial Intelligence Centre targeted financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list where USD, ACH, or wire rails are used, and relevant UK OFSI sanctions where UK clearing occurs. PEP status must be assessed in accordance with FICA section 1; enhanced due diligence applies to domestic, foreign, and international PEPs and their family members and close associates. Source of funds and source of wealth statements must be documented for any person flagged as PEP, sanctioned, or subject to adverse negative media. Screening records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eservices name clearance application, accessed through the CIPC Online transactional services portal ('Reserve Company Name' module).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A private company name may be in any of the twelve official South African languages and must include or be followed by an approved private company suffix such as 'Proprietary Limited', 'Pty Ltd', or '(Pty) Ltd'. CIPC processes names in Latin script only; any name originating in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin alphabetic characters, and the transliterated form becomes the registered name. Supporting name justifications should be submitted in English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, building society, mutual bank, savings bank, credit union
Financial services provider, investment services, securities services, fund manager
Medical scheme, health insurance, medical insurance
University, technikon, college, school, academy if implying an educational institution
Government, state, national, province, municipality, minister, president, official organ
South Africa, RSA, SA if implying official state patronage
Trust, co-operative, foundation, chamber of commerce if implying regulated or representative status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before expiry, the applicant should file an online extension re-request or a fresh CIPC name reservation using the same proposed name; CIPC may require a renewed name search. If CIPC rejects a name, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Companies Tribunal under sections 32(5) and 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and regulation 183 of the Companies Regulations 2011, using Form CTR 143, within 20 business days of the refusal notice. The application must state the rejection reference, the grounds for review, and a proposed alternative name. The Companies Tribunal may order CIPC to register the name or remit the matter for reconsideration; judicial review in the High Court remains available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for a low-risk overseas public relations and communications agency. The registered office under Companies Act section 23(3) must be a physical street address in South Africa where notices and legal process can be served; a pure mailbox or post-office-box-only arrangement is not sufficient. A serviced-office arrangement with a physical reception, mail handling, and an authorized acceptance-of-service capability is acceptable. SARS and CIPC will require evidence that the office is actively monitored and that the foreign owner has a designated local representative.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated: approximately 25% likelihood of a SARS or CIPC verification visit or documentary query within the first 18 months. The likelihood rises to 40% if annual returns, tax registration, or beneficial ownership filings are delayed, or if all directors are non-residents. No statutory public relations licence is required, so inspections will be substance-based rather than licence-based.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC e-Services, file CoR 9.1 name reservation application, ensure the name does not conflict with registered names or trademarks, and pay the statutory name reservation fee. Approved names are reserved for 6 months.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of applicant director's identity document or passport
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried (e.g., undesirability or similarity), file a new CoR 9.1 with alternative names or lodge an objection response within 20 business days via CIPC e-Services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI) in compliance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008, including share capital structure, director powers, and registered office address; complete Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1); execute by each incorporator with a witness signing each page.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director forms (CoR 14.2) from each director
Consent to act as auditor/company secretary if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any statutory defect identified by CIPC within 10 business days of notification and resubmit the amended CoR 14.1; no new fee if the file reference is preserved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with CIPC and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed CoR 14.1 and MoI electronically via CIPC e-Services using the previously reserved name reference; pay the prescribed incorporation fee (approximately ZAR 175); upon approval CIPC issues the Registration Certificate and company registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query, submit a correction letter via e-Services within 20 business days; rectify document typography or affix missing signatures and resubmit using the same transaction number to avoid new filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and Employer Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, obtain an income tax reference number, register for VAT (compulsory if annual taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million; voluntary if above ZAR 50,000 per 12-month period), and register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL.
required_dossiers: Bank account details (where VAT refunds required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS returns an incomplete registration, review and resupply the outstanding documents via eFiling; request a SARS branch appointment if the online verification fails; penalties may be objected to under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and FICA Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution (e.g., Standard Bank, First National Bank, Nedbank, Absa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate banking account in the company's name, submit the Certificate of Incorporation, MoI, resolution of directors approving the account, and provide FICA-compliant verification documents; sign mandates for electronic banking, retainer ACH and wire payment rails.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution approving bank account
Certified IDs of directors and authorised signatories
Utility bill or lease agreement evidencing registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FICA vetting fails or the bank queries beneficial ownership, supplement source-of-funds declarations and updated certified documents; alternatively select a second banking institution to avoid SME onboarding delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Occupational Health and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality (e.g., City of Johannesburg) and Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the zoning rights of the registered office for office-based professional services; obtain an Occupancy Certificate for the leased premises; register the company as an employer for COIDA (Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act) with the Compensation Fund.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed for registered office
Occupancy certificate / certificate of completion from building control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For zoning contraventions, apply for a consent use or departure under the municipal town planning scheme; for DOEL/COIDA non-compliance, submit corrective registration and mitigate penalties via voluntary disclosure to the Compensation Fund.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://secure.sarsefiling.co.za; main site at https://www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the entity with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain the company registration number. CIPC exchanges registration data with SARS, after which the (Pty) Ltd must verify its SARS tax profile via eFiling, update registered details, appoint authorised representatives, and ensure the income tax reference number is active. Separate applications must be made for VAT registration when the taxable supply threshold is met or expected to be met, and for other payroll-related taxes where applicable. Non-resident-owned entities must declare shareholder and beneficial-owner information and comply with exchange-control reporting through the authorised dealer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid mismatch election are available; a South African (Pty) Ltd is automatically a separate entity-level taxpayer. Relevant statutory elections include voluntary VAT registration under s 23 of the VAT Act where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000, VAT group registration under s 50 of the VAT Act for eligible wholly-owned group entities, and certain foreign exchange and foreign tax credit elections under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in the preceding 12 months or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in the following 12 months; voluntary registration is available once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 per annum.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a general real-time fiscal e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping mandate. Electronic tax invoices are accepted where they preserve authenticity, integrity and readability under s 20(5) of the VAT Act. SARS eFiling is the statutory digital channel for VAT returns, and goods export clearances must be lodged electronically through SARS Customs using the SAD500 declaration; a cleared electronic SAD500 is essential evidence for export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for zero-rating under s 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the supplier removes or delivers movable goods through a SARS customs-controlled area to a non-resident destination and full export evidence is retained. Indirect exports under s 11(1)(b) may be zero-rated where the non-resident recipient exports the goods on behalf of the supplier and the supplier obtains and retains proof of export. Offshore services, including international media relations, crisis PR, and communication consultancy supplied to non-resident clients, are zero-rated under s 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act only where the services are not physically rendered in South Africa, are not connected with South African movable or immovable property, and the non-resident recipient is not physically present in South Africa during performance. International transport and related ancillary services require separate statutory authorization.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD500) cleared by SARS Customs
Bill of lading, airway waybill or equivalent transport document evidencing export
Inward remittance certificate or bank foreign exchange receipt matching the export invoice
Commercial invoice, packing list and sale or service contract confirming the non-resident counterparty and export destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits require the complete evidential bundle, matching of foreign currency receipts, and compliance with the 180-day exchange-control repatriation deadline. Missing or defective documentation invalidates zero-rating, triggering an additional VAT assessment at 15% plus interest and understatement penalties under s 223 of the Tax Administration Act of up to 200% of the tax shortfall for gross negligence or intentional evasion. Deliberately false export documentation or fraudulent refund claims expose the entity to criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, and summary VAT refund clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and the nationwide network of Authorised Dealers (ADs — South African commercial banks licensed under the Banks Act, 1990), exercising delegated exchange control powers under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), as amended, and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa operates a liberalised but administratively supervised convertibility regime. For current account transactions — the central earnings stream of this overseas PR and international media relations firm (retainer fees, crisis-communications retainers, media placement reimbursements, software/streaming subscriptions) — the ZAR is freely convertible against all major currencies: an Authorised Dealer may effect payment or receipt of foreign currency on production of standard commercial documentation (invoice, contract, statement of work) without SARB/FinSurv prior approval. For capital account transactions, inward non-resident equity investment into the ZA (Pty) Ltd is fully liberalised (no prior approval; post-transaction reporting via FinSurv's Electronic Monitoring/EM system), while outward capital transfers, offshore shareholder loans above the AD's discretionary threshold, and certain disposals remain subject to AD due diligence and, for high-value or complex routing, FinSurv approval. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to: (i) dividend withholding tax at the statutory 20% (reduced under most double-taxation treaties, commonly 5–10% for corporate shareholders); (ii) proof of capital importation (EM record formerly generated by Form G5) for loan principal or capital repatriation; (iii) a completed CRS/FATCA self-certification confirming the beneficial shareholder's tax residence; and (iv) solvency-and-liquidity certification in the board resolution. There are no material convertibility restrictions for the expected monthly retainer inflows from OECD-based clients.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The full export consideration for cross-border services (including PR retainers and administrative service fees rendered to non-resident clients) must be received into the South African banking system — either into a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorised Dealer or by conversion into ZAR — within 180 days from the date of completion of the service/invoice date (the AD may approve a documented extension up to 365 days where settlement cycles justify it). No mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts: 0% of gross proceeds must be converted to ZAR; the exporter may lawfully retain 100% of proceeds in USD, EUR, or GBP in the FCA and disburse directly from that account for permissible purposes. However, the entire gross proceeds must remain within the AD's oversight, and all inbound/outbound FCA movements must be supported by underlying service invoices, recorded in the entity's exchange-control file, and reported through the AD's monthly balance-of-payments returns to FinSurv. The service exporter is required to maintain, for a minimum of five years, a complete documentary trail consisting of executed retainer agreements, monthly invoices, proof-of-receipt SWIFT confirmations, and the AD's record of FCA utilisation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility rating. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, Currenxie and similar) are neither licensed banks nor authorised dealers in South Africa under the Banks Act, 1990, and the Exchange Control Regulations. They cannot independently hold the ZA (Pty) Ltd's ZAR account or act as a receiving agent for export service proceeds, because full export proceeds must land with a South African AD within the 180-day surrender window. Routing recurring US/EU client retainer income through an offshore EMI would be characterised as non-remitted export proceeds and could trigger FinSurv enforcement, AD account restriction, and exchange-control penalties. Acceptable use of an EMI is limited to ancillary outbound disbursements — e.g., settling small overseas subcontractor or media-vendor invoices — provided the underlying transaction is disclosed to the SA AD, covered by valid invoices, and funded from the AD-held FCA or an approved conversion. As a primary inbound clearing rail, offshore EMIs are not viable; the correct architecture is direct SWIFT/wire into the AD's USD/EUR correspondent clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For South African resident directors and resident natural-person shareholders, FICA-compliant remote onboarding is generally available using Smart ID / automated Home Affairs identity verification, provided the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register is filed and the directors' identity results are returned electronically. For non-resident directors, foreign corporate shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners, physical presence is effectively mandatory under the major banks' risk appetite: the individual must attend an in-branch interview, or a video-based KYC interview with cryptographic identity verification plus an independent documentary review by the bank's specialist international onboarding unit. Minimum documentary prerequisites for the foreign dimension are: notarised/apostilled passport copies, a bank reference letter from the home institution evidencing at least 12 months of satisfactory conduct, confirmation of the non-resident director's tax identification in the home jurisdiction, and completion of the bank's FICA Part A/B forms and CRS self-certification. Among the tier-1 banks, Absa and FNB currently provide the most accommodating hybrid remote/notarial route; Standard Bank presumes physical attendance for non-resident directors, with the interview conducted at its Johannesburg or Cape Town corporate banking centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with no SARS tax reference and no verifiable South African footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified passport copy bearing apostille (Hague Convention) or notarisation; (2) SARS Non-Resident Tax Reference Number confirmation letter or withholding-tax registration acknowledgement; (3) CIPC CO-R 6.1 foreign-director consent and power of attorney; (4) at least 12 months' bank reference from the home-jurisdiction institution; (5) sworn affidavit of lawful source of wealth and source of funds for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered offshore beneficial ownership — e.g., a non-resident holding company incorporated in a low-tax jurisdiction owning 100% of the ZA (Pty) Ltd
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Beneficial Ownership Register filed with CIPC under the Companies Act Beneficial Ownership Regulations, disclosing every natural person holding ≥5%; (2) full corporate-organisation chart through every intermediate entity to the ultimate individuals; (3) certified register of members of the offshore parent; (4) legal opinion from the offshore counsel identifying each natural-person UBO and the control pathway; (5) bank-issued FATCA/CRS self-certification signed by every signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound equity capital (foreign venture or shareholder funding) triggering source-of-wealth and capital-importation scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed share-subscription agreement and board resolution authorising the capital call; (2) SWIFT MT103 confirmation from the remitting bank quoting purpose code 'GIV' (direct inward investment); (3) AD-issued Electronic Monitoring (EM) capital-import record; (4) funding-source evidence (shareholder's audited financial statements, disposal statement, or employment/remuneration records); (5) signed undertaking to report future loan principal and dividend repatriations to the AD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening alerts on an overseas client, media vendor, or subcontractor receiving PR retainers or disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Refinitiv World-Check / Accuity sanctions and PEP screening report with no confirmed matches; (2) where an unresolved alert persists, the counterparty's completion of a beneficial-ownership and ultimate-controller declaration; (3) contractual anti-sanctions, anti-money-laundering and anti-bribery warranties from the overseas client; (4) detailed purpose-of-payment evidence (fee invoices, statement of work, media-placement breakdowns); (5) the bank FICA officer's written no-objection memorialising the relationship rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity materially disproportionate to registered capital and headcount (characteristic of a low-asset, high-intangible service exporter)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Project-level fee-invoice register with PO references and retainer periods reconciling line-by-line to inbound wires; (2) operating-expense trail for media buying, subcontractor fees and software subscriptions with valid vendor invoices; (3) monthly management accounts certified by the financial director; (4) SARS EMP201/VAT-201 filings demonstrating substance; (5) CIPC annual financial statements filed for at least the initial two financial years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Future dividend repatriation to the non-resident shareholder flagged at onboarding as a probable annual occurrence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) SARS dividend withholding tax (DWT) declaration and payment confirmation at 20% or applicable treaty rate; (2) board minute resolving the dividend with solvency-and-liquidity test certification; (3) completed CRS income-class disclosure for the shareholder; (4) DTR.01 dividend tax return and proof of remittance through the AD; (5) three-year projected dividend schedule supporting the AD's ongoing risk classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign direct equity injection by the non-resident shareholder is routed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the remitting bank to the chosen AD's inbound clearing desk, with the remittance instruction quoting BOP purpose code 'GIV' (direct inward investment). The AD's documentation checklist comprises: the share-subscription agreement, the board resolution, the payer's confirmed bank details on BIC directory, and the completed inward-investment notification through which the AD issues an EM (Electronic Monitoring) capital-import record that functions as the definitive proof for future dividends, loan repayments and capital repatriation. No SARB or FinSurv prior approval is required for the equity inward transfer; the AD screens the payer, effects conversion at the ruling market rate where the entity elects ZAR, and credits the capital-escrow or operational account. Where the injection is structured as a shareholder loan, the loan agreement must be lodged with the AD, the funds must land through the same AD to preserve the capital-import record, and the term/interest rate must satisfy the AD's arm's-length review; proceeds cannot be offset offshore. For recurring monthly retainer inflows from US clients (who prefer ACH in the domestic US rail), the client should initiate a SWIFT wire into the AD's USD correspondent account at its New York clearing agent rather than a pure ACH transfer; the AD will then advise the USD FCA, preserving the export-remittance record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operating disbursements are executed through the following clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 correspondent wire for all vendor payments exceeding ZAR 50 000 — media placement, crisis-communications subcontractors, travel, and licensing — supported by the vendor invoice and a plain-language purpose-of-payment descriptor; (2) commercial letters of credit (ICC UCP 600) advised by the AD, used only where physical deliverables are imported (printed campaign materials, event and production supplies), priced at approximately 0.20–0.45% of the LC value; (3) commercial cards for low-value subscription purchases (digital ad platforms such as Google, Meta and programmatic DSPs, news-monitoring databases, cloud/SaaS subscriptions) with monthly aggregation reporting to the AD; (4) standing-order batched SWIFT payments for recurring monthly retainer payouts to reputable overseas sub-agencies, each batch supported by an invoice register. Under the current FinSurv discretionary framework, the AD may process cumulative current-account outward payments up to ZAR 1 billion per entity per calendar year without FinSurv reference; above that threshold FinSurv prior approval is required, a level this entity will not approach. The AD must file monthly balance-of-payments returns capturing every outbound transaction, and the entity must retain the full commercial voucher file for a minimum of five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (covered forwards) quoted by an Authorised Dealer for up to 12 months against committed export service invoices and retainer receivables, with rollover permitted on AD approval

Cross-currency swaps (ZAR/USD and ZAR/EUR) permissible for hedging the capital-account exposure of the inbound equity injection and future dividend repatriation, subject to FinSurv derivative reporting through the AD
Vanilla FX option contracts (purchased European options) from the AD for hedging the USD- and EUR-denominated retainer receivable book, with premiums payable in ZAR

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — expressly offshore instruments available to non-resident counterparties; not available to this South African resident entity, which must use deliverable onshore forwards within the AD's net open-position constraints

Natural hedging through the retention of export proceeds in USD/EUR Foreign Currency Accounts, permitting direct settlement of overseas vendor invoices from the FCA without conversion into ZAR and thereby eliminating conversion spread and the need for derivative overlays on the operating cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, annual return notice and filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the first anniversary of date of incorporation, and annually on the same anniversary thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of ZAR 125 per month per annual return; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in a compliance notice and administrative strike-off/deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Shareholding Register Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (submitted as part of the annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual anniversary filing; any transfer or change of beneficial ownership must also be reported to CIPC within 5 business days of the change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify is an offence under the Companies Act 2008; CIPC may issue a compliance notice and a fine or imprisonment of up to 12 months may be imposed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Financial Statement Supporting Data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the tax year / financial year; provisional tax payments are due semi-annually, but the annual return deadline controls the final assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may impose administrative non-compliance penalties up to ZAR 250 per month for late filing, raise an estimated assessment, and pursue collection; interest runs on unpaid tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit is triggered if the company's public interest score is 350 or more under the Companies Act regulations; the score is calculated using number of employees, turnover, third-party liabilities, and beneficial owners. A private company below the threshold may elect an independent review instead of a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board, or IFRS for SMEs as adapted by the South African Accounting Standards Board; both frameworks are recognised under the Companies Act 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return to CIPC must confirm the beneficial ownership register and any shareholding transfers. The register must be kept up-to-date at the registered office; any transfer or change must be recorded in the UBO register and reported to CIPC within 5 business days. The annual confirmation reaffirms the existing UBO details or reports changes made during the year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 - $500 per annum for standard registered office and company secretarial service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 - $7,500 per annum for a full audit of a small-to-medium PR agency; an independent review typically ranges from $1,200 - $2,800 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (28% for years of assessment ending before that date); secondary tax on companies was abolished, with the company's retained earnings exempt from non-resident shareholders' tax except the 20% Dividends Tax at distribution.
